'''unprejudicedly''' (un-prej′ọ̈-dist-li), ''adv.'' In an unprejudiced manner; impartially. [Rare.]
{{smaller block|Let us consider this evidence as ''unprejudicedly'' and carefully as we can. {{right|''Amer. Nat.'', XXIII. 897.}}}}

'''unprejudicedness''' (un-prej′ọ̈-dist-nes), ''n.'' The state of being unprejudiced. ''Clarke.''

'''unprelate''' (un-prel′āt), ''v. t.'' To depose from the dignity of prelate; depose from the episcopate. ''Bp. Hacket'', Abp. Williams, ii. 120. (''Davies.'')

'''unprelatical''' (un-prẹ̄-lat′i-kal), ''a.'' Unlike or unsuitable to a prelate. ''Clarendon'', Civil War, I. 257.

'''unpremeditable''' (un-prẹ̄-med′i-ta̤-bl), ''a.'' [< ''un-''<sup>1</sup> + *''premeditable'', < ''premedit''(''āte'') + ''-able''.] '''1.''' Not capable of being premeditated or previously thought of. ''Imp. Dict.''—'''2.''' Unforeseen; unlooked for; unexpected.
{{smaller block|A capful of wind . . . comes against you . . . with such ''unpremeditable'' puffs.
{{right|''Sterne'', Sentimental Journey, The Fragment.}}}}

'''unpremeditate†''' (un-prẹ̄-med′i-tāt), ''a.'' Unpremeditated.
{{smaller block|In sudden and ''unpremeditate'' prayer I am not always I; and, when I am not myself, my prayer is not my prayer.
{{right|''Donne'', Sermons, xi.}}}}

'''unpreparedly''' (un-prẹ̄-pãr′ed-li), ''adv.'' In an unprepared manner or condition; without due preparation.

'''unpreparedness''' (un-prē-pãr′ed-nes), ''n.'' The state of being unprepared, unready, or unfitted; want of preparation.

'''unprepossessed''' (un-prē-pọ-zest′), ''a.'' Not prepossessed; not biased by previous opinions; not prejudiced.

'''unprepossessing''' (un-prē-pọ-zes′ing), ''a.'' Not prepossessing; not attractive or engaging; unpleasing: as, a person of ''unprepossessing'' appearance.

'''unprescribed''' (un-prē-skrībd′), ''a.'' Not prescribed; not authoritatively laid down; not appointed: as, ''unprescribed'' ceremony. ''Bp. Hall'', Letter from the Tower.

'''unpresentable''' (un-prē-zen′ta-bl), ''a.'' Not presentable; not fit for being presented or introduced to company or society; not in proper trim; unfit to be seen.
{{smaller block|I could better eat with one who did not respect the truth or the laws than with a sloven and ''unpresentable'' person.

'''unpressed''' (un-prest′), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not pressed.

readings.c3s3:
¶
'''unprevailing''' (un-prẹ̄-vā′ling), ''a.'' Of no force; unavailing; vain.
{{smaller block|<poem>Throw to earth
This ''unprevailing'' woe.</poem>
{{right|''Shak.'', Hamlet, i. 2. 107.}}}}

'''unpreventable''' (un-prẹ̄-ven′ta̤-bl), ''a.'' That cannot be prevented.

'''unpreventableness''' (un-prẹ̄-ven′tạ-bl-nes), ''n.'' The character or state of being unpreventable; inevitableness. ''Mind'', No. 35, 1884.

'''unprevented''' (un-prē-ven′ted), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not prevented; not hindered.—'''2†.''' Not preceded by anything.
{{smaller block|<poem>Grace . . .
Comes ''unprevented'', unimplored, unsought.</poem>
{{right|''Milton'', P. L., iii. 231.}}}}

'''unpriced''' (un-prīst′), ''a.'' '''1.''' Having no price set or indicated.
{{smaller block|The books offered for sale are ''unpriced'', and customers are invited to make their offers.
{{right|''Athenæum'', No. 3177, p. 355.}}}}

'''2.''' Priceless; above or beyond price.
{{smaller block|<poem>Thine ageless walls are bonded
With amethyst ''unpriced''.</poem>
{{right|''J. M. Neale'', tr. of Bernard of Cluny.}}}}

'''unpride†''' (un-prīd′), ''v. t.'' To strip or divest of pride or self-esteem.
{{smaller block|Be content to be ''unprided''. ''Feltham'', Resolves, i. 33.}}

'''unprejudicate†''' (un-prẹ̄-jö′di-kāt), ''a.'' Not prepossessed by settled opinions; unprejudiced.
{{smaller block|A pure mind in a chaste body is the mother of wisdom and deliberation, . . . sincere principles and ''unprejudicate'' understanding. {{right|''Jer. Taylor'', Holy Living, ii. 3.}}}}

'''unprejudicateness''' (un-prẹ̄-jö′di-kāt-nes), ''n.'' The character or state of being unprejudicate. ''Hooker'', Eccles. Polity.

'''unprejudice''' (un-prej′ọ̈-dis), ''n.'' Freedom from prejudice.
{{smaller block|Mr. Carlyle is an author who has now been so long before the world that we may feel towards him something of the ''unprejudice'' of posterity.
{{right|''Lowell'', Study Windows, p. 121.}}}}

'''unprejudiced''' (un-prej′ọ̈-dist), ''a.'' [Early mod. E. also ''unprejudizd''; < ''un-''<sup>1</sup> + ''prejudiced''.] '''1.''' Not prejudiced; free from undue bias or prepossession; not preoccupied by opinion; impartial: as, an ''unprejudiced'' mind.
{{smaller block|The meaning of them may be so plain that any ''unprejudiced'' and reasonable man may certainly understand them.
{{right|''Tillotson.''}}}} 2. Not warped by or proceeding from prejudice: as, an ''unprejudiced'' judgment.—'''3.''' Not hurt; unimpaired; undamaged.
{{smaller block|<poem>A pair of most dissembling hypocrites
Is he and this base Earle, on whom I vowe,
Leauing King Lewis ''vnpreiudizd'' in peace,
To spend the whole measure of my kindled rage.</poem>
{{right|''Heywood'', 2 Edw. IV. (Works, ed. Pearson, 1874, I. 102).}}}}

'''unprejudicedly''' (un-prej′ọ̈-dist-li), ''adv.'' In an unprejudiced manner; impartially. [Rare.]
{{smaller block|Let us consider this evidence as ''unprejudicedly'' and carefully as we can. {{right|''Amer. Nat.'', XXIII. 897.}}}}

'''unprejudicedness''' (un-prej′ọ̈-dist-nes), ''n.'' The state of being unprejudiced. ''Clarke.''

'''unprelate''' (un-prel′āt), ''v. t.'' To depose from the dignity of prelate; depose from the episcopate. ''Bp. Hacket'', Abp. Williams, ii. 120. (''Davies.'')

'''unprelatical''' (un-prẹ̄-lat′i-kal), ''a.'' Unlike or unsuitable to a prelate. ''Clarendon'', Civil War, I. 257.

'''unpremeditable''' (un-prẹ̄-med′i-ta̤-bl), ''a.'' [< ''un-''<sup>1</sup> + *''premeditable'', < ''premedit''(''āte'') + ''-able''.] '''1.''' Not capable of being premeditated or previously thought of. ''Imp. Dict.''—'''2.''' Unforeseen; unlooked for; unexpected.
{{smaller block|A capful of wind . . . comes against you . . . with such ''unpremeditable'' puffs.
{{right|''Sterne'', Sentimental Journey, The Fragment.}}}}

'''unpremeditate†''' (un-prẹ̄-med′i-tāt), ''a.'' Unpremeditated.
{{smaller block|In sudden and ''unpremeditate'' prayer I am not always I; and, when I am not myself, my prayer is not my prayer.
{{right|''Donne'', Sermons, xi.}}}}

'''unpremeditated''' (un-prẹ̄-med′i-tā-ted), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not previously meditated or thought over.
{{smaller block|<poem>My celestial patroness who deigns
Her nightly visitation unimplored,
And dictates to me slumbering, or inspires
Easy my ''unpremeditated'' verse.</poem>
{{right|''Milton'', P. L., ix. 24.}}
Profuse strains of ''unpremeditated'' art.
{{right|''Shelley'', The Skylark.}}}}
'''2.''' Not previously purposed or intended; not done by design: as, an ''unpremeditated'' offense. ='''Syn. 1.''' {{smaller|Unstudied, impromptu, offhand, spontaneous. See ''extemporaneous''.}}

'''unpremeditatedly''' (un-prẹ̄-med′i-tā-ted-li), ''adv.'' In an unpremeditated manner; without premeditation; undesignedly.

'''unpremeditation''' (un-prẹ̄-med-i-tā′shọn), ''n.'' Absence of premeditation; undesignedness.
{{smaller block|The Anecdotes of Sierra seem to us to fail in that larklike ''unpremeditation'' which belongs to the lyric.
{{right|''The Atlantic'', LXV. 563.}}}}

'''unpreparation''' (un-prep-a-rā′shọn), ''n.'' The state of being unprepared; want of preparation; unpreparedness. ''Sir M. Hale'', Afflictions.

'''unprepared''' (un-prẹ̄-pãrd′), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not prepared. {{smaller|(''a'') Not fitted or made suitable, fit, or ready for future use: as, ''unprepared'' provisions. (''b'') Not brought into a right, safe, or suitable condition in view of a future event, contingency, accident, attack, danger, or the like; not put ous: as, an ''unprepared'' speech; ''unprepared'' speaking. (''d'') Not brought into a particular mental state; not trained: as, an ''unprepared'' student.}}

'''2.''' In ''music'', specifically of a dissonant tone, not held over from a preceding chord or otherwise prepared; reached by a skip.

'''unpreparedly''' (un-prẹ̄-pãr′ed-li), ''adv.'' In an unprepared manner or condition; without due preparation.

'''unpreparedness''' (un-prē-pãr′ed-nes), ''n.'' The state of being unprepared, unready, or unfitted; want of preparation.

'''unprepossessed''' (un-prē-pọ-zest′), ''a.'' Not prepossessed; not biased by previous opinions; not prejudiced.

'''unprepossessing''' (un-prē-pọ-zes′ing), ''a.'' Not prepossessing; not attractive or engaging; unpleasing: as, a person of ''unprepossessing'' appearance.

'''unprescribed''' (un-prē-skrībd′), ''a.'' Not prescribed; not authoritatively laid down; not appointed: as, ''unprescribed'' ceremony. ''Bp. Hall'', Letter from the Tower.

'''unpresentable''' (un-prē-zen′ta-bl), ''a.'' Not presentable; not fit for being presented or introduced to company or society; not in proper trim; unfit to be seen.
{{smaller block|I could better eat with one who did not respect the truth or the laws than with a sloven and ''unpresentable'' person.
{{right|''O. W. Holmes'', Emerson, p. 184.}}}}

'''unpressed''' (un-prest′), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not pressed.
{{smaller block|My pillow left ''unpress’d.'' ''Shak.'', A. and C., iii. 13. 106.}}
'''2.''' Not enforced. ''Clarendon'', Great Rebellion.

'''unpresuming''' (un-prẹ̄-zū′ming), ''a.'' Not presuming; modest; humble; unpretentious.
{{smaller block|Modest, ''unpresuming'' men.
{{right|''V. Knox'', To a Young Nobleman.}}}}

'''unpresumptuous''' (un-prẹ̄-zump′t̮ū-us), ''a.'' Not presumptuous or arrogant; humble; submissive; modest.
{{smaller block|Lift to Heav’n an ''unpresumptuous'' eye.
{{right|''Cowper'', Task, v. 746.}}}}

'''unpretending''' (un-prẹ̄-ten′ding), ''a.'' Not pretending to or claiming any distinction or superiority; unassuming; modest.
{{smaller block|To undeceive and vindicate the honest and ''unpretending'' part of mankind. {{right|''Pope.''}}}}

'''unpretentious''' (un-prẹ̄-ten′shus), ''a.'' Not pretentious; making no claim to distinction; modest.

'''unpretentiousness''' (un-prẹ̄-ten′shus-nes), ''n.'' The character or state of being unpretentious; unassumingness; modesty.
{{smaller block|The journal is . . . none the less pleasant for its simplicity and ''unpretentiousness.''
{{right|''Athenæum'', No. 3240, p. 322.}}}}

'''unprettiness''' (un-prit′i-nes), ''n.'' The state of being unpretty; want of prettiness.
{{smaller block|She says it is not pretty in a young lady to sigh; but where is the ''unprettiness'' of it?
{{right|''Richardson'', Sir Charles Grandison, III. 51.}}}}

'''unpretty''' (un-prit′i), ''a.'' Not pretty; lacking prettiness, attractiveness, elegance, or charm.
{{smaller block|His English is blundering but not ''unpretty.''
{{right|''Mme. D’Arblay'', Diary, II. 155. (''Davies.'')}}}}

'''unprevailing''' (un-prẹ̄-vā′ling), ''a.'' Of no force; unavailing; vain.
{{smaller block|<poem>Throw to earth
This ''unprevailing'' woe.</poem>
{{right|''Shak.'', Hamlet, i. 2. 107.}}}}

'''unpreventable''' (un-prẹ̄-ven′ta̤-bl), ''a.'' That cannot be prevented.

'''unpreventableness''' (un-prẹ̄-ven′tạ-bl-nes), ''n.'' The character or state of being unpreventable; inevitableness. ''Mind'', No. 35, 1884.

'''unprevented''' (un-prē-ven′ted), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not prevented; not hindered.—'''2†.''' Not preceded by anything.
{{smaller block|<poem>Grace . . .
Comes ''unprevented'', unimplored, unsought.</poem>
{{right|''Milton'', P. L., iii. 231.}}}}

'''unpriced''' (un-prīst′), ''a.'' '''1.''' Having no price set or indicated.
{{smaller block|The books offered for sale are ''unpriced'', and customers are invited to make their offers.
{{right|''Athenæum'', No. 3177, p. 355.}}}}

'''2.''' Priceless; above or beyond price.
{{smaller block|<poem>Thine ageless walls are bonded
With amethyst ''unpriced''.</poem>
{{right|''J. M. Neale'', tr. of Bernard of Cluny.}}}}

'''unpride†''' (un-prīd′), ''v. t.'' To strip or divest of pride or self-esteem.
{{smaller block|Be content to be ''unprided''. ''Feltham'', Resolves, i. 33.}}<noinclude><references/></noinclude>
